title: What a lower limit that lifts off zero means for one event: coverage, flip-flopping and the Baxter et al. conventions
question: For one event on b~6e-4, what 90% two-sided lower edge do FC, toy-calibrated t~_mu, Delta chi^2 and Cowan asymptotics give; does LZ's digitised Fig. 6 lower edge (0.31-0.38 events) match any; what is the coverage of two-sided intervals reported without a discovery threshold vs flip-flopping; how often does a background-only raster scan lift some lower limit off zero; how should 'lower limit non-zero' be read?
headline_result: Every 90% two-sided construction gives a lower edge of 0.105 (FC = toy-calibrated = Delta chi^2) or 0.16-0.18 events (Cowan asymptotics), not LZ's digitised 0.31-0.38 (which equals the 68% edge; Delta chi^2=1 reproduces Table I's 1.0 +1.4 -0.7); spectral information only lowers the edge; FC coverage is exact and LZ's no-threshold policy costs no coverage (naive Delta chi^2 dips to 0.694), but a background-only scan lifts some 90% lower limit off zero in 25-35% of experiments vs global p = 0.0047, so 'lower limit non-zero' means only p_local < 0.10
model_or_mechanism: single-bin Poisson n=1 with exact FC Neyman construction, toy-calibrated t~_mu, Cowan boundary-aware asymptotic cdf; one-event unbinned likelihood e^{-s}(s+beta); exact coverage enumeration incl. 3-sigma-threshold reporting policies; 12-bin raster-scan toy with P008 NR-band background; smeared-calibration mechanism mu_lo(f); Gaussian-regime PCL check
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens the reading of non-zero lower limits as evidence; LZ's coverage is correct)
confidence: high for interval/coverage algebra (exact Poisson); medium for scan rate (toy bins) and digitised-edge comparison
